item.title: Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit
item.description: Lazio forward Andrea Pinamonti celebrates after scoring his team's second goal (tiziana fabi) Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points. Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M'Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win. With 28 points from 10 games, Lazio moved three clear of Inter after they lost the Milan derby. Unbeaten Roma sit third on 24 points and Como climbed back to fourth with a 1-0 win over rock-bottom Venezia. Lazio last won Serie A in 2000 and this is the best start to a league campaign in the club's history. As has been the case in recent home matches, Lazio played in front of largely empty sections of the Stadio Olimpico, with many ultras and supporters continuing their boycott in protest against owner and president Claudio Lotito, whom they accuse of failing to invest sufficiently in the squad. Como's victory at home over lowly Venezia on Sunday was a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions. The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha converted in the 43rd minute for the French international's first goal of the season. "This is the type of match we found hard to win last season," Da Cunha told DAZN. Cesc Fabregas's side had slipped to fifth when AC Milan beat champions Inter 3-1 on Saturday. Como moved one point behind Roma, who beat Udinese 5-2 on Saturday. "This victory is really important in terms of our maturing process," said Fabregas. "Our state of mind is irreproachable," added the 39-year-old Spaniard. Como resume their Champions League campaign against Lens on Wednesday. In a season in which Italian teams have struggled in Europe, Como have the best record of the Serie A clubs in the Champions League, sitting ninth in the 36-team standings, with six points from three games. Como, who were playing in Italy's third division as recently as 2021, beat Manchester United 4-1 in the last round of European matches. jr/dmc/mw

Hamlin, meanwhile, has zero DNFs and a 9.1 average finish, the best in the Cup Series. Despite that contrast, Larson holds a 73-point championship advantage with two races remaining. Another response was much less interested in comparing NASCAR with other sports. “Playoffs are for stick and ball sports, go watch them, because you aren’t race fans,” the user wrote. That reaction shows a familiar divide among NASCAR fans. I remember the 9-7 New York Giants taking out the undefeated New England Patriots. I guess the NFL is broken too? — Blake R. Others pushed back, arguing that motorsports cannot simply be judged by the same standards as stick-and-ball sports. One fan brought television ratings into the discussion, questioning why NASCAR should copy formats used by the NBA and NFL when the sports have different audiences and competitive structures. The response was blunt: “There’s a reason why in motorsports they don’t crown off relevancy and who won the latest race.” The exchange captures the divide among fans. Some want NASCAR to reward season-long consistency, while others believe the playoff system creates the uncertainty and pressure that make the championship compelling. So, is NASCAR’s championship format broken? Or is it simply doing what a playoff system is designed to do: leave the title undecided until the final races, even when the regular-season numbers suggest another driver has been stronger? item.description: Oct 31, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) after missing a free throw against the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter of game seven of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. And she made it clear that she expects Atlanta to be right back in the mix next year. Valkyries Win First Title The Dream took a 2-1 lead in the series before dropping two straight games. They forced a Game 7 by beating the Valkyries 80-69 in Game 6 on Thursday, with Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard combining for 44 points. item.title: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint
item.description: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New Orleans Saints are having a rough 2026 season, and heading into their Week 8 bye, the Saints are in last place in the NFC South, tied at 2-5 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . While they might not be out of the divisional race just yet, the Saints really need things to turn around soon, or else this season will end in disappointment. Fortunately, during their bye week, the Saints got some great news on a key injured player. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jordyn Tyson, the team's first-round rookie wide receiver who's been on injured reserve for the entire season thus far, is getting very close to returning. There's even a chance he's good to go for Week 9. Saints finally get good news on rookie WR Jordyn Tyson "Saints first-pick Jordyn Tyson could return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him as early as next week vs. the Browns , per sources," Schefter reports. "But even if it's not then, he is not far away from playing." The Saints are getting close to seeing their first-round, No. 8 overall rookie wide receiver make his NFL debut. He suffered a hamstring injury leading up to the regular season, causing him to land on IR. He's since missed seven games, and with the Week 8 bye giving the Saints an early-season week off, it makes sense that Tyson missed those first seven weeks. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Rushing him back before the bye would've made no sense, especially for a team that's likely still trying to climb out of the bottom of the NFC. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele have been great in his absence, but getting Tyson back would be huge for the Saints this season. Even if they don't make the playoffs, seeing what Tyson can offer is still very important to the Saints. While it's too soon to tell if Tyson will be good to go for Week 9, his status will be one to monitor this upcoming week, as his chances of returning from IR are better than ever. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek during a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Nov. 2, 2025. Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Before Sunday afternoon’s rivalry matchup with the Cleveland Browns, the Pittsburgh Steelers announced their inactives, a group that includes receiver Ben Skowronek (calf). Skowronek was a limited participant in the Steelers’ Wednesday, Thursday and Friday practices. That sense of belonging stands out in motorsports, where sponsorship is usually visible through paint schemes, firesuits, and appearances. A partnership can put a company’s colors on the car and connect a driver with fans. Red Bull’s athlete community adds something else: a NASCAR driver can find common ground with a Formula 1 racer, or with an athlete from a completely different sport, simply because they belong to the same program. Red Bull’s NASCAR return gives Connor Zilisch a wider platform The hat comes with a long history behind it. Red Bull fielded its own Cup Series team from 2007 through 2011 before leaving the sport. The brand returned in January 2025, when Trackhouse announced Red Bull as the team’s official energy drink. Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen were already Red Bull athletes by then, van Gisbergen since 2016 and Zilisch since 2024. Zilisch has said he was surprised when Red Bull presented him with his helmet and hat that year. The 2025 deal put Red Bull colors on van Gisbergen’s car for five Cup races and on Zilisch’s Cup debut at Circuit of the Americas. For 2026, Red Bull expanded its role, splitting 25 primary sponsorship races between Zilisch’s No. 88 and van Gisbergen’s No. 97. The timing matters for Zilisch. He won 11 O’Reilly Series races for JR Motorsports last season, then moved up to Trackhouse for his rookie Cup campaign. In August, Hendrick Motorsports announced a multi-year deal that will put him in the No. 48 Chevrolet, replacing Alex Bowman, beginning in 2028. Zilisch is set to remain in Trackhouse’s No. 88 through 2027. There is also a practical side to being around experienced athletes. Scott Speed, a former Formula 1 driver who raced for Red Bull’s own Cup team from 2008 to 2010, has been part of Zilisch’s development since 2022, helping with simulator work and advice. Speed and van Gisbergen were also the ones who surprised Zilisch with his Red Bull-designed helmet at Watkins Glen in 2024. That mix of stock car and Red Bull experience gives the young driver a perspective few of his peers can match. The conversation eventually returned to Zilisch’s own headwear when the interviewer pointed out that his hat carried the Trackhouse logo. “It’s got the Trackhouse logo.” “I know. Yeah, this one’s custom. If you get caught, like, that must have been Shane’s. Yeah, exactly. I’ll always blame it on Shane.” The joke offered a lighter ending to an otherwise revealing exchange. To fans, a Red Bull hat might look like any other piece of sponsor merchandise. To Zilisch, it represents access to a much smaller community, one that connects athletes across disciplines and opens doors beyond the racetrack. The logo is familiar, but the privilege attached to wearing it is anything but ordinary. item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) drives against Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga (24) at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs All-Star guard De'Aaron Fox accomplished something in Saturday's 121-111 victory over Minnesota that has rarely happened in franchise history. Fox finished with 22 points on 8-of-10 shooting from the field, a team-high eight rebounds (including two on the offensive end) and a team-best seven assists in 35 minutes, marking just the fifth game in which a Spur has had 20-plus points, eight-plus rebounds and seven-plus assists while shooting 80% from the floor. Jakob Poeltl (2022), Gene Banks (1983, 1985) and Billy Paultz (1978) are the other players to do it. "Just trying to be efficient, trying to affect the game in different ways, get downhill," said Fox, who notched his first 20-point game of the season in helping the Spurs win their fourth in a row to improve to 4-2. Through six games, Fox is averaging 16.5 points on 57.6% shooting, 4.8 rebounds, a team-high 7.0 assists and 1.5 steals. "We know to go to him," said All-Star center Victor Wembanyama, who led the Spurs with 43 points. "We know to put the ball in his hands. He knows to go get the ball. And he's been reacting defensively too. So, it's a true point guard." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. For Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, the show must go on. According to those on the ground, the message received was as follows: “Warning. City of Riyadh is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors, and follow the instructions of Civil Defense.” This was then accompanied by a social media post from Turki Alalshikh, the man responsible for bringing Mbilli vs. Alvarez to Riyadh, which said, quite simply: “May God protect Riyadh and all who are in it.” Of course, the biggest challenge for Alvarez and Mbilli would have been maintaining focus and concentration, both throughout fight week and on the night itself. Perhaps, in the end, the immediate danger in front of them was sufficient to override greater dangers, but still, for both, it must have been tough. For all the distraction offered by the incoming fists of an opponent, even the most emotionally detached boxer would struggle to shake from their mind the volatility of the situation outside the ring. Then again, boxing is nothing if not a microcosm of life in a “warzone.” In fact, every time two boxers enter a ring and throw punches with the aim to cause damage, there is an ever-present, unavoidable risk of death . They know it, we know it, yet still the show goes on; still they get in the ring and fight. They do so because, by then, they will have managed to convince themselves that death and serious injury are things that happen to other people. They do so because it is their job, all they know. Ordinarily, the more a boxer fights, the more comfortable they start to feel, both in the ring and in terms of that belief. With a boxer like Alvarez, for example, there can be no man better equipped to handle business at a time of peril and uncertainty. One look at his career, which now spans 69 professional fights, and you will find a fighter who has frequently and with relish put himself in harm’s way at every turn. From turning pro as a child at the age of 15 to boxing Floyd Mayweather at 23 and then later rising to light heavyweight to fight the likes of Sergey Kovalev and Dmitry Bivol, Alvarez has shown time and time again an ability to find comfort in situations lesser men would avoid. Even last night’s fight against Mbilli, which saw Alvarez in the position of challenger, was one many experts considered a risk . Mbilli, they said, was a potential problem for Alvarez, stylistically, what with his physical strength, his high output, and his capacity to march forward undeterred. If, as assumed, Alvarez was indeed past his best, or no longer capable of fighting with the intensity of old, the last thing he needed at this point in his career was a hungry champion like Christian Mbilli. Christian Mbilli was unable to withstand the pressure and presence of "Canelo" Alvarez. FAYEZ NURELDINE via Getty Images There were signs of this, too, during the early stages of their fight on Saturday. The opening two rounds, for instance, were rounds in which Mbilli seemed happy to be on the front foot letting his hands go with confidence. Until he was told not to, or was stung by something coming back, the Cameroonian-Frenchman had no issue forcing the pace, aware that Alvarez, for all his brilliance, had not stopped an opponent since 2021. That fact alone gave Mbilli hope, or at least the fuel to keep pushing forward and punching. When he did, it was easy to see why some had backed him to win. This was especially the case whenever he threw punches in bunches, starting them low to the body before bringing them up to the head. In such moments Mbilli provided the image judges traditionally like to see on fight night: An aggressive boxer coming forward and outworking his opponent against the ropes. It wasn’t only the judges, mind you. There was a sense as well that “Canelo” rather liked the image — that is, the feeling — of Mbilli fighting in this manner, all huff and puff. Before long, it became quite apparent he was able to read the telegraphed attacks of the champion and that, rather than being bothered by them, he was instead wanting to invite more and more of them. This led to Alvarez retreating to the ropes of his own volition and, in Round 3, beating his chest, shaking his head, and demanding Mbilli come toward him and keep throwing. He knew by now, having got the measure of Mbilli in the opening two rounds, how to tame the man in front of him. To do so, he had to put himself in harm’s way. Otherwise, it might have been difficult to penetrate Mbilli’s guard, so long were his forearms. “Canelo” tried, and had success with right hooks around the side, but clearly his preference was to have Mbilli open up first and then fire, typically with jabs and some wonderfully-picked right uppercuts. How comfortable he looked, too, up against the ropes, beckoning Mbilli toward him. There, despite the threat, he appeared not only composed but safe. He read the trajectory of every imminent attack and often, particularly as the fight progressed, had a counter for Mbilli from a defensive position. In fact, the mere threat of a response was what ultimately reduced the number of attacks coming from Mbilli. item.title: Alcaraz wins Vienna Open to maintain perfect record
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz is a seven-time Grand Slam winner [Getty Images] Carlos Alcaraz powered to a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur to win the Vienna Open and maintain his perfect record in ATP 500 events this year. The Spanish second seed triumphed 6-1 6-4 in 87 minutes for his 16th straight win at that level in 2026. Alcaraz has won 26 straight matches at ATP 500 events - a run that goes back to the 2025 Barcelona Open, where he lost to Holger Rune. The 23-year-old's run this year includes titles in Doha and Tokyo. "I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better, more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me," said Alcaraz. "I'm just really happy that at the end I found my way, played great, and obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me." Alcaraz started the match strongly, with his groundstrokes causing De Minaur problems. De Minaur took five of the seven games in the first set to deuce, but it was Alcaraz's quality at key moments that made the difference as he secured three breaks of serve. Alcaraz continued to apply pressure in the second set, and while De Minaur's trademark defence helped the 27-year-old Australian save three break points, he could not fend off championship point. After a gripping rally, Alcaraz whipped a forehand winner across court to seal victory, before raising both arms in celebration. The win was Alcaraz's seventh against De Minaur, maintaining his perfect head-to-head record. item.title: How Dart revived career with help of Wimbledon champion
item.description: In the hour following her first WTA title win, Britain's Harriet Dart had little time to respond to the stream of congratulatory messages flashing up on her phone. Most pressing was making a call to her proud parents, Nick and Susie, who had been watching the final with friends at their local tennis club in north London, and her sister Phoebe. The next person she spoke to was 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli. Dart has been coached by the French former world number seven since the start of the season on a part-time basis, and she credits Bartoli for helping her achieve what some thought was beyond her. On Sunday, with Bartoli watching from home, the world number 115 won the Guangzhou Open in China by beating rising Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger. "It's been quite incredible to work with Marion, and I was really fortunate she was open to working with me," Dart, 30, told BBC Sport in a video call from Guangzhou. "I'm obviously at a very different stage of my career to someone who is, say, 20. But I still feel I have a lot to improve and there are gains to be made. "She really believes in me - that means the world to me. Seeing a Grand Slam champion having that belief has made me believe a lot more in myself." Britain's Dart wins first WTA title in 'wild week' When Dart started working with Bartoli, she was ranked outside the top 160. The pair live close to each other in Dubai and spend training blocks together there when Dart is not on the road. Dart and Bartoli, who has a young family, are not travelling full-time together on tour, but there have been opportunities for them to work on the ground, particularly during this year's Grand Slam tournaments. Dart says 42-year-old Bartoli still hitting the ball "really well" in practice is another benefit of the partnership. In Guangzhou, Dart was accompanied by her fitness trainer Dario Gonfiantini and boyfriend Stephen Falck. Without her coach, Dart had to largely rely on figuring things out herself - with the help of Bartoli sending over observational notes. Dart is projected to rise to 83rd on Monday after lifting the Guangzhou trophy to cap a stunning second half of the season. Dart has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 23 victories from 34 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career. item.title: Barcelona star addresses Manchester United links
item.description: Barcelona star addresses Manchester United links Barcelona star Fermín López has issued a response to the surprise recent speculation linking him with a move to the Premier League, with struggling Manchester United. Midfielder Fermín is for his part in the midst of what has been another thoroughly productive opening to the new campaign. Just last night, the Spanish international secured Man of the Match honours, after notching a goal and two assists en route to a 6-1 Barca drubbing of Deportivo Alavés. This took Fermín’s season tally to 12 direct goal contributions in 13 appearances between La Liga and the Champions League. Amid an ongoing search for added dynamism in their engine room ranks, the aforementioned Manchester United are in turn understood to have earmarked Barca’s all-action midfielder as the ideal profile. Speaking to the media in the aftermath of his side’s victory over Alavés on Saturday, however, Fermín was keen to play down his Old Trafford links: “Manchester United links? I don’t pay attention to that kind of news. I want to stay here at Barça as long as possible. I hope to end my football career at this club and retire here.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Chinese state TV fails to air Real Madrid match after Mbappe row
item.description: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe scored in Sunday's La Liga clash against Racing Santander, but viewers in China were unable to see the goal after state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast the match (ANDER GILLENEA) Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT but was not broadcast on either of CCTV's two sports channels, AFP reporters saw. None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga have been broadcast live on public television so far. A viral video in recent days showed Mbappe referring to Mao as a "dictator", prompting the body overseeing CCTV to say it would halt broadcasts of the top Spanish league. Mbappe, Real and La Liga later all said sorry for his remarks, and China's foreign ministry said it took the player's apology "seriously". Asked by AFP before the weekend, La Liga said that Chinese television had previously shown all games live, without specifying which platforms hosted the broadcasts. AFP journalists did find live broadcasts of matches on Migu, a digital streaming service owned by the state-owned China Mobile telecom network. That included Barcelona's 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday. However, the Racing Santander–Real Madrid match did not appear to be broadcast on Sunday on Migu. China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV, had said it had moved on Monday to suspend La Liga broadcasts, adding that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the furore. The viral video showed Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme about him he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. Mbappe later apologised for his "ill-judged" comments, La Liga said it "deeply" regretted them, and Real followed suit. CCTV's sports website later reported that CMG had acknowledged the apologies, but it remains unclear whether talks to defuse the situation have begun. China is a huge market for European football, with CCTV also carrying matches from the Premier League as well as the German, French and Italian top flights. Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that the club had "done our part" to put the controversy behind them. It is taboo in China to crack jokes about Mao, who died in 1976 and whose drastic policies are blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths. Major Chinese brands cancelled sponsorship deals with Mbappe after his comments. Various overseas sports leagues and players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. item.title: New York Jets vs Las Vegas Raiders: Breece Hall headlines Jets’ inactives
item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Running back Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets is checked for injury during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Breece Hall will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Las Vegas Raiders today. Hall will be inactive for the fifth consecutive week after he suffered a quadriceps injury against the Detroit Lions in the Jets’ third game of the 2026 season. The Jets are hopeful Hall will finally get back into the lineup next week against the Kansas City Chiefs. Hall’s absence has created an opportunity for Braelon Allen at running back, and Allen has taken full advantage. In the four games Allen has started in Hall’s absence this season Allen has put together two 100+ rushing yards games. Overall, Allen has averaged 4.6 yards per carry this season while already posting career highs in rushing yards with 418 and yards from scrimmage with 493. Allen has arguably been a more effective back than Hall, and he has presumably earned a larger role in the Jets’ offense even when Hall is back in the lineup. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Breece Hall David Bailey Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Tim Patrick Kohl Levao Max Mitchell Notable among those names is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. Unfortunately that signing has not worked out for Wright or the Jets. Wright has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

item.title: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule sends message to Huskers fans after third straight loss
item.description: Matt Rhule had a message for Nebraska Cornhuskers fans in his postgame news conference Saturday night, after the Washington Huskies won 17-10 at Memorial Stadium in Nebraska’s annual Blackout Game. The loss marked the third straight game in which Nebraska held a lead in the fourth quarter and walked off beaten. The skid has turned a 5-0 start into a 5-3 record, with the three losses coming by a combined 13 points. The No. 7 Indiana Hoosiers erased a 17-6 fourth-quarter deficit to win 20-17 on Oct. 10, the Oregon Ducks followed with a 17-14 win a week later, and Washington finished the set on Halloween night. “I certainly understand how frustrated everyone is that this has happened three games in a row. But all I can do is show up tomorrow and get back to work for Illinois,” Rhule said. Oct 11, 2025; College Park, Maryland, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule walks on the field during the game against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Washington finished with a season-low 267 yards and punted on eight of its nine possessions, and Nebraska carried a 7-3 lead into the fourth quarter. Kyle Cunanan then missed a 36-yard field goal that would have made it 10-3. Washington backup quarterback Demond Williams Jr., who entered early in the fourth quarter, kept the winning drive alive with a 24-yard completion to Chris Lawson on fourth-and-18. Lawson caught the go-ahead touchdown two plays later with 1:30 left. Anthony Colandrea’s third interception of the night was returned 48 yards for a touchdown by Alex McLaughlin on the next possession, and John Hohl’s 42-yard field goal with 31 seconds left only trimmed the margin. “Three turnovers and a missed field goal are not a recipe to win,” Rhule said. Matt Rhule shares his message to Nebraska fans after three straight losses. https://t.co/wSOb0BriNa — Hail Varsity (@HailVarsity) November 1, 2026 Why Matt Rhule’s fourth-quarter warning keeps coming true Oct 11, 2025; College Park, Maryland, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule on the field before the game against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Rhule identified the same issue at his Monday news conference on Oct. 19, two days after the Oregon loss. “We won’t win the games we want to win until we win the fourth quarter,” Rhule said. Nebraska had an open week before Washington and still lost the fourth quarter 14-3 to an offense that had punted on nearly every possession until then. Rhule’s message Saturday paired an acknowledgment of the frustration with a promise of work, and the fourth-quarter problem he described after Oregon has now cost Nebraska a third straight game it led late. Nebraska plays at the Illinois Fighting Illini on Friday at 8 p.m. ET on Fox. item.title: NFL rumors: How Myles Garrett trade helped get Jeffery Simmons deal over finish line for Bears, Titans
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images NFL rumors: How Myles Garrett trade helped get Jeffery Simmons deal over finish line for Bears, Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears ’ blockbuster acquisition of Jeffery Simmons reportedly took shape because of another massive NFL trade. Chicago and the Tennessee Titans used the Myles Garrett deal as a blueprint for their negotiations, helping both sides agree on the defensive tackle’s value. The Bears had been searching for a defensive difference-maker, and Simmons emerged as their target. Tennessee initially resisted interest in its four-time Pro Bowler, who had signed a lucrative contract extension earlier this year. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Bears general manager Ryan Poles contacted Titans GM Mike Borgonzi again Tuesday night. The teams then used the Garrett trade as their framework for determining compensation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cleveland previously received Jared Verse and three draft picks from the Los Angeles Rams for Garrett. Tennessee reportedly valued Verse as equivalent to a first-round selection when comparing the packages. That helped establish the price for Simmons. Chicago surrendered its 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-rounder, while receiving Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round selection. The Titans also studied other blockbuster trades involving Matthew Stafford and Russell Wilson before deciding additional draft capital could accelerate their rebuild. Chicago approached the negotiations differently. The Bears examined recent Super Bowl champions and identified the importance of elite interior defensive linemen. Simmons fit that profile, giving Chicago an established presence alongside its existing defensive talent. For Tennessee, the return provides valuable flexibility as the franchise builds around its younger players. The organization had previously dismissed trade interest in Simmons. Ultimately, the Garrett deal helped both front offices settle on a price. Chicago gained an immediate defensive upgrade, while Tennessee secured premium draft assets for its future. item.title: Jaguars vs. Colts Week 8 inactives: Jonathan Taylor officially active
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) enter Sunday's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts (2-5) with little in the way of mystery. As the Jaguars continue their season with Super Bowl aspirations, the Colts appear to be going in the opposite direction. Indianapolis traded two of their best franchise players: guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . The team could still trade star running back Jonathan Taylor , but he was deemed active for the contest. Either way, a full rebuild is in store for the Colts, who also canned their general manager a couple of weeks ago. PREVIEW: Why Jaguars' 11 straight home wins vs Colts don't matter to Liam Coen Before the game, the Jaguars elevated linebacker Jamal Hill from their practice squad to the active roster via standard elevation. Hill was signed to the practice squad last week. Jaguars Week 8 inactives vs. Colts: Antonio Johnson ruled out ahead of game Before the game, the Jaguars announced that safety Antonio Johnson (ankle) would be ruled out for Sunday's contest. Johnson was injured during the team's Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans . Meanwhile, the franchise is welcoming back cornerback Montaric Brown, who missed Week 6 after re-injuring the ailment in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles . Brown missed Week 4 with the same ailment. Despite being listed as questionable, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is active. Jaguars Week 8 inactives vs. Colts: S Antonio Johnson WR CJ Williams CB Alijah Huzzie LB Jamal Hill DE Wesley Williams DT Albert Regis Jonathan Taylor set to play despite trade interest A storyline ahead of the contest on the opposite side of the field is Taylor's status and whether the team will offload him for picks a la Buckner and Nelson. So far, reports around the league have indicated the Colts are listening to offers and are willing to deal the back. But there's been no indication the Colts are shopping Taylor. They aren't desperate to move him. Because of the trade interest, many speculated whether Taylor would be active. Indy just answered that: they're keeping the franchise RB active for today's game against Jacksonville. The question remains: how much will Taylor play? item.title: Did Stephon Castle Get Hurt? Why Spurs’ Star Scored 0 Points vs. Timberwolves
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 08: Stephon Castle #5 of the San Antonio Spurs handles the ball during the second quarter against the New York Knicks in Game Three of the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on June 08, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Getty The San Antonio Spurs got the chance to take on a Minnesota Timberwolves team that is without an injured Anthony Edwards on Saturday. The Wolves are still talented, but this was a key opportunity for the Spurs to pick up a Western Conference win against a shorthanded foe. The Spurs didn’t pass that chance up. They took care of business in a 121-111 win on Saturday night. There was plenty of good from the Spurs, starting with a monster stat night from Victor Wembanyama. Wemby scored 43 points on 17-for-34 shooting from the floor, including 3-for-8 from deep, as well as 6-for-9 on free throws. He added seven rebounds, four assists, six blocks and a steal. The Spurs also got 25 points, seven rebounds and six assists out of Dylan Harper, and De’Aaron Fox had 22 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. The one oddity came from Stephon Castle: He didn’t score a point. Did Stephon Castle Get Hurt? Stephon Castle didn’t appear to get injured during Saturday’s game, but he did enter proceedings at less than 100%. The Spurs had added him to the injury report less than 24 hours before the game. He was listed as questionable due to a migraine. Castle did eventually get deemed available to play. Why Stephon Castle Scored 0 Points Whatever migraine Castle was dealing with couldn’t have helped, and he also got in a bit of foul trouble that stopped him from finding a rhythm. He ended up playing 22 minutes to score his 0 points. Castle shot 0-for-4 from the field, including 0-for-2 from 3-point range. He didn’t get to the foul line. At least Castle contributed five rebounds and four assists with a steal, although he did have three turnovers. The Spurs played Harper, Fox, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson all big minutes. It seems they might’ve been aware all along that Castle might need a bit more time on the bench than usual. It’s going to be something worth watching with Castle going forward, both in the short-term and long-term. The first thing is simply whether Castle is listed on the injury report before the next game, because that suggests this is something the Spurs might have to manage. Migraines can also re-emerge later on as an issue, so if that’s something that nags Castle going forward, it’s certainly less than ideal. For now, the Spurs can feel good they got a nice win, and Castle can do his best to recover and recharge before the next time out. item.title: Bengals Get Major Update on Potential Blockbuster Trade for Saquon Barkley
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 27: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs onto the field prior to the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The Cincinnati Bengals‘ run game has been underwhelming through their first six games this season. There’s a lot that factors into it. There’s no secret that Cincinnati is a pass-first team and would be regardless of who’s in the backfield. When you have Joe Burrow at quarterback with wide receivers like Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside, you’re going to want to throw the ball. At the same time, Cincinnati has really struggled when trying to establish the run with Chase Brown or Samaje Perine. With the trade deadline set for Nov. 10, rumors have circulated about the Bengals potentially targeting a running back. Cincinnati has been linked to several running back targets, including Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor and Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley. Bengals Get Major Update on Barkley A trade for either player would be a blockbuster, and on Saturday, we found out that the Colts are truly open to moving Taylor. As for Barkley, despite the Eagles sitting at 2-5, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport revealed Sunday morning that Philadelphia has no intention of trading the star running back. Via ESPN.com : “Saquon Barkley will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline, sources told NFL Network, putting an end to speculation that the star running back could be on the move with the Philadelphia Eagles trending toward being out of contention.” Is Barkley Playing on Sunday Night? The Eagles will travel to Washington to take on the Commanders in a massive divisional matchup that could have major implications for their season. As of now, all indications point to Barkley being active and ready to go. He made it clear that playing wasn’t much of a question when speaking to the media Friday. “One day I’m not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don’t want to look back and be like, ‘I could’ve gave it a chance and I didn’t,'” Barkley said. “I like playing football. So if I have an opportunity to play, I’m going to try my best to play.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Bengals Get Major Update on Potential Blockbuster Trade for Saquon Barkley appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Buffalo Bills Week 8 inactives vs. the Baltimore Ravens
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Dee Alford #23 of the Buffalo Bills lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and the Baltimore Ravens are set to face off in what is a huge AFC matchup. With a win, the Bills move to 6-1 and maintain their edge over the New England Patriots in the AFC East. With a loss, they lose pace not only with New England, but with the Kansas City Chiefs in the race for the AFC’s top overall seed. Baltimore’s stakes are higher. Presently, they are 4-3, but they find themselves in fourth place in a surprisingly strong AFC North division. A win moves them to 5-3 and puts them right in the thick of things. However, a loss drops them to 4-4 and, depending on some other AFC results, could put them in a terrible position in the first week of November. Both teams have some key players returning from injury this week, but both teams also have key contributors who won’t be available. Here are the inactive players for each team this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR Skyler Bell After suiting up in the last two games thanks to DJ Moore’s absence, Bell is back to a healthy scratch with Moore returning. Joshua Palmer, who also missed Buffalo’s last game with an injury, is healthy and active this week, as well. T Spencer Brown After tweaking his back in practice this week, Brown was listed as questionable. Now, we know he’s out. Tylan Grable will likely start in his place. Rookie Jude Bowry is active for the first time this season. G Ar’Maj Reed-Adams The rookie seventh-round pick is once again a healthy scratch. DL Greg Gaines The veteran injured his calf in practice this week, and while he was listed as questionable, he’s not going to play today. Fortunately for Buffalo, Ed Oliver is back in action. OLB Mike Danna Rookie T.J. Parker was listed as quesitonable, so there was at least a shot that the veteran Danna would play this week. However, Parker is going to play, so Danna is once again a healthy scratch. CB Dee Alford With yesterday’s practice squad elevations of Geno Stone and A.J. Woods, as well as the signing of Te’Cory Couch to the active roster, this was something we expected. Couch will likely see plenty of time in the slot, although Woods is definitely an option there, as well. S Jalon Kilgore Looks like it’s Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone at safety to replace CJ Gardner-Johnson this week. I thought Kilgore would have an opportunity this week. I thought incorrectly. item.description: Iraola’s midfield has rediscovered its aggression and intensity just in time for Sunday’s visit of Arsenal to Anfield Alexis Mac Allister found himself in a strong position to apply pressure on Liverpool over a new contract before Atlético Madrid’s visit to Anfield last month , although only in the physical sense of being up on stage to preview the game in front of a mass audience. He has become the indispensable part of Liverpool’s central midfield and to an extent that, merely seven weeks on from that headline-grabbing Champions League press conference, it is not only Mac Allister who thinks he deserves a contract extension. item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
